elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “Customer, its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
The clause does not state that paid-up licences are perpetual and instead allows the licence to end upon expiration or termination of the Agreement.
Although the licence is described as irrevocable, it may end upon expiration or termination of the Agreement, and there is no separate protection for paid-up licences.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The licence may end upon any expiration or termination permitted by Section 3; the operative language does not limit termination to uncured material breach.
No transfer or successor right is included.

elements.element: Licence extends to Customer's affiliates on written notice.
elements.evidence: Affiliates are covered automatically without notice, which is broader than coverage upon written notice.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no transfer right for an M&A successor.

result.reason: The redline adds Affiliate and contractor coverage but does not establish the required paid-up or subscription licence protections and contains no successor transfer right. Tying an otherwise “irrevocable” licence to any expiration or termination under an unseen Section 3 is materially broader than termination solely for uncured material breach. The edits are targeted and preserve the existing use restrictions, but they do not achieve either complete position and therefore are not minimal to a complete acceptable level.
